words.ex: Everyone in the class has a different opinion about the new rule.

dialogue.t: Do you think students should have a longer lunch break?
Yes, I do. In my view, thirty minutes isn't enough time.
Why do you think that?
The main reason is that we need time to eat and relax before afternoon lessons.
Can you give me an example?
For instance, yesterday I had to eat my sandwich in five minutes because the queue was so long.
That's a good point, but wouldn't the school day be longer?
Maybe, but in my view, happy students learn better.

grammar.title: Giving and supporting an opinion
grammar.ar: نستخدم In my view لنقول رأينا، وهي تعني «من وجهة نظري». بعدها نشرح السبب بعبارة The main reason is that ... ثم نُتبعها بجملة كاملة فيها فاعل وفعل. ونستخدم For instance (مثل for example) لإعطاء مثال يدعم رأينا. انتبه: لا تقل In my opinion I think لأن المعنى يتكرر.
examples: In my view, students should learn to cook at school.
The main reason is that cooking is a useful life skill.
For instance, you can make healthy meals instead of buying fast food.

words.ex: Our school uniform is a blue shirt and grey trousers.
Supporters of the idea say it will save money.

dialogue.t: Today's topic is school uniforms. Should students have to wear them?
Supporters argue that uniforms make everyone equal, so nobody feels left out.
That's true. However, critics say uniforms stop students from expressing themselves.
I see what you mean. But uniforms also save time in the morning.
Maybe. However, critics say they're often uncomfortable and expensive.
Supporters argue that they're cheaper than buying lots of fashionable clothes.
Hmm, that's a fair point. Maybe the answer is a more comfortable uniform!

grammar.title: Reporting both sides with 'that' clauses
grammar.ar: عندما ننقل آراء الآخرين نستخدم Supporters argue that ... أو Critics say that ... ثم جملة كاملة. لاحظ أن الفعل يأتي بدون s لأن الفاعل جمع (supporters, critics). ونستخدم However في بداية الجملة، وبعدها فاصلة، لنعرض الرأي المعاكس، ومعناها «لكن / ومع ذلك».
examples: Supporters argue that uniforms help students focus on learning.
However, critics say that students should choose their own clothes.
Some parents argue that uniforms are too expensive.

words.ex: We get maths homework three times a week.
I need to revise for my science test tomorrow.
In my free time, I play football with my cousins.
Too many tests can cause a lot of stress.
You should practise your English every day.
The deadline for the project is next Monday.

dialogue.t: So, should teachers give homework every day?
I'd argue that a little homework is useful. It helps us remember what we learned.
What's more, it teaches us to plan our time.
Nevertheless, too much homework can cause a lot of stress.
True. Some of my friends stay up until eleven to finish it.
Exactly. I'd argue that students also need free time for sport and family.
Nevertheless, without any homework, we might forget everything before the test!
OK, so maybe the answer is less homework, not no homework.

grammar.title: Adding and contrasting ideas
grammar.ar: عبارة I'd argue that تعني «أرى أنّ» وهي طريقة مهذبة وقوية لطرح الرأي، وI'd هي اختصار I would. نستخدم What's more لإضافة سبب آخر، ومعناها «علاوة على ذلك». أما Nevertheless فمعناها «ومع ذلك» ونستخدمها لعرض فكرة معاكسة، وتأتي عادة في بداية الجملة وبعدها فاصلة.
examples: I'd argue that homework helps students become more independent.
What's more, it gives parents a chance to see what we are learning.
Nevertheless, students need time to rest after school.

words.ex: Our teacher doesn't allow food in the classroom.

dialogue.t: Our school bans phones during the day. Do you agree with the rule?
Not really. If phones were allowed, students would be able to call their parents in an emergency.
But if phones were allowed, students would play games in class.
Not if teachers made clear rules. We could use them only for research.
I'm not sure. If I had my phone in class, I'd check my messages all the time!
Ha! On balance, though, I think phones are more useful than harmful.
On balance, I'd keep them in lockers but let students use them at lunch.
That sounds like a fair compromise.

grammar.title: Second conditional for imaginary situations
grammar.ar: نستخدم الجملة الشرطية الثانية للحديث عن موقف غير حقيقي أو متخيَّل الآن: If + الماضي البسيط، ثم would + الفعل الأساسي. مثلاً: If phones were allowed (لكنها في الواقع ممنوعة). لاحظ أننا نستخدم were مع جميع الضمائر في هذا التركيب. وعبارة On balance تعني «بعد الموازنة بين الإيجابيات والسلبيات».
examples: If phones were allowed, students would take photos of the board.
If I had a phone in class, I would find it hard to focus.
On balance, I think a total ban is too strict.

dialogue.t: It could be argued that zoos protect endangered animals.

OK, but it could be argued that zoos help children learn about wildlife.
I disagree, because we can learn a lot from documentaries too.
Maybe, but seeing a real elephant is different from watching a screen.
True, but the elephant has much less space than in its natural habitat.
It could be argued that good zoos have large, natural enclosures.
Some do, but I still think wild animals belong in the wild.

grammar.title: Impersonal opinions and polite disagreement
grammar.ar: عبارة It could be argued that تعني «يمكن القول إنّ»، ونستخدمها لطرح فكرة بشكل رسمي دون أن نقول إنها رأينا الشخصي. ولكي نرفض فكرة بأدب نقول I disagree, because ... ثم نذكر السبب مباشرة. انتبه: نقول I disagree وليس I am disagree، لأن disagree فعل ولا نحتاج معه am.
examples: It could be argued that zoos keep animals safe from hunters.
I disagree, because animals need to live freely.
It could be argued that some animals live longer in zoos.

words.ex: Our opening statement must be short and clear.
In the closing statement, you repeat your best arguments.

Her speech was very persuasive, so we all voted for her.
The audience clapped at the end of the debate.
Let's vote for the best team.

dialogue.t: Good morning, everyone. Today our team is arguing that school should start an hour later.
And our team is arguing that the start time should stay the same.
Teenagers need more sleep, and tired students can't concentrate. For all these reasons, we believe a later start is better.
But a later start means finishing later, so there's less time for clubs and homework.
Clubs could start later too, so nobody would lose anything.
To sum up, changing the timetable would cause problems for families and teachers.
To sum up, a later start would make students healthier and happier.
Thank you. Now it's time for the audience to vote!

grammar.title: Concluding a debate
grammar.ar: في الكلمة الختامية نستخدم To sum up بمعنى «باختصار / خلاصة القول» لنلخّص أهم أفكارنا. ونستخدم For all these reasons بمعنى «لكل هذه الأسباب» لنربط الأسباب التي ذكرناها بالنتيجة النهائية. تأتي العبارتان في بداية الجملة وبعدهما فاصلة، ولا نضيف فيهما أفكاراً جديدة بل نكرر أقوى الحجج فقط.
examples: To sum up, homework is useful, but only in small amounts.
For all these reasons, we believe phones should stay in lockers.
To sum up, our team thinks zoos do more good than harm.

And there's a special offer that ends tomorrow. That's another trick!
Right. It's trying to make us buy them quickly without thinking.

dialogue.t: Good morning. We're here to present our product, the Smart Lunchbox.
Welcome. So, what problem does your product solve?
Our product solves the problem of cold, boring school lunches. It keeps food warm for six hours.
Interesting. Who are your customers?
Mainly parents of children aged six to fourteen. We've already sold two hundred lunchboxes online.
Impressive. How much money do you need?
We are asking for five thousand pounds in return for a 15% share of our company.
That sounds reasonable. I'd like to hear more about your plans.

Yes, please. I'm afraid there's a problem with this phone charger I bought here last week.
I'm sorry to hear that. What's wrong with it?
It's faulty. It only charges my phone sometimes.
I apologise for that. Do you have your receipt?
Yes, here it is. Would it be possible to get a refund?
Of course. Or, if you prefer, we can replace it with a new one.
A new one would be great, thank you. Would it be possible to test it before I leave?

words.ex: At just fifteen, Sara became an entrepreneur selling homemade candles.

You need hard work and patience to succeed.

dialogue.t: Thanks for talking to us, Omar. You're only fourteen and you already run a business. How did you get started?
I started making phone cases with my 3D printer at home. My friends loved them, so I began selling them online.
That's amazing! What was the hardest part?
The hardest part was finding time for homework and orders. I was always busy!
Did you ever want to give up?
Yes, once. Some cases broke, and customers complained. But I fixed the design and kept going.
What advice would you give to other young entrepreneurs?
Start small, listen to your customers, and don't be afraid of mistakes.

grammar.title: Past simple questions

Why did you choose this product?

words.ex: I had culture shock when I first moved to London.
It took me a while to get used to the cold weather.

words.ar: مشتاق إلى الوطن / يحنّ إلى بيته
words.ex: She felt homesick and missed her family every day.
Shaking hands is a common custom in many countries.
Children usually adapt to new schools quickly.
At first, the food tasted strange to me.

dialogue.t: How was your first year in Canada, Faisal?
Honestly, it was hard at the beginning. I had real culture shock.
Really? What was the most difficult thing?
The weather! It took me a while to get used to the snow and the short days.
I can imagine. Did you feel homesick?
Yes, a lot. I used to call my mum every night, but now I only call her at the weekend.
So you've adapted well. What about the food?
I used to hate it, but now I actually love poutine!

grammar.title: Used to vs. Get used to
grammar.ar: نستخدم used to + الفعل في المصدر للحديث عن عادة في الماضي لم تعد موجودة الآن، مثل: I used to live in Jeddah. أما get used to + اسم أو فعل بـ ing فتعني «يعتاد على» شيء جديد. لاحظ أن to في get used to لا يأتي بعدها المصدر، فنقول: It took me a while to get used to waking up early.
examples: I used to feel shy, but now I talk to everyone.
It took me a while to get used to the new timetable.
She is getting used to living in a big city.

words.ex: The main ingredients of kabsa are rice, meat and spices.
My grandmother adds lots of spices to make the food tasty.
This recipe has been in our family for many years.
Jareesh is a traditional dish in Saudi Arabia.
Mandi is usually served with a spicy tomato sauce.
You need to stir the soup so it doesn't burn.

dialogue.t: What's your favourite traditional dish?
Definitely jareesh. My grandmother makes the best one!
I've never tried it. How is it made?
It's made from crushed wheat. First, the wheat is washed, and then it is cooked for hours with chicken or meat.
For hours? That sounds like a lot of work.
It is! It has to be stirred again and again, so it becomes soft and creamy.
And what do you eat it with?
It is usually served with fried onions on top and a cup of laban.

grammar.title: Present Simple Passive
grammar.ar: المبني للمجهول في المضارع البسيط يتكوّن من is/are + التصريف الثالث للفعل (V3). نستخدمه عندما يكون الاهتمام بالطعام وطريقة تحضيره وليس بالشخص الذي يطبخه، مثل: The rice is cooked with meat. ويمكن وضع كلمات مثل usually أو often بين is/are والفعل.
examples: The meat is cooked for hours on a low heat.
Kabsa is usually served with salad and yoghurt.
The dates are mixed with flour and butter.

words.ex: My cousin is fluent in English and French.
It's great to practise with a native speaker.
English pronunciation can be tricky because of silent letters.
Reading books helps you build your vocabulary.
Many children in Dubai are bilingual.
Don't worry if you make mistakes. That's how we learn.

dialogue.t: Why do you think learning languages is important?
Well, learning a language helps you make friends from other countries.
That's true. It also helps you understand films without subtitles!
Ha! Yes. What's the hardest thing about English for you?
The hardest thing about English is the pronunciation. Words like 'through' and 'though' confuse me.
For me, it's spelling. But I'm not afraid of making mistakes anymore.
Good for you. Would you like to learn another language too?
Yes, Japanese! I want to be fluent one day.

grammar.title: Gerunds as Subjects
grammar.ar: عندما يأتي الفعل في بداية الجملة كفاعل نضيف إليه ing، مثل: Learning a language helps you... ويُعامل كمفرد، لذلك نقول helps وليس help. وبعد عبارة The hardest thing about ... is نضع اسماً أو فعلاً بـ ing.
examples: Learning a language helps you get a better job.
Speaking with native speakers is very useful.
The hardest thing about English is remembering the spelling.

words.ex: Our flight was delayed for three hours.
We went to the lost luggage desk to find my bag.
Hurry up, or we'll miss our flight!
Please show your boarding pass at the gate.
The train was cancelled, so we asked for a refund.
We can check in at the hotel after two o'clock.

dialogue.t: Excuse me. I'm sorry to bother you, but my suitcase didn't arrive.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Which flight were you on?
Flight SV 117 from Riyadh. I was wondering if you could help me find it.
Of course. Would you mind showing me your boarding pass?
No, not at all. Here you are.
Thank you. It looks like your bag is still in Riyadh. It will arrive on the next flight.
That's a relief. Would you mind sending it to my hotel?
No problem. Just write the hotel address on this form, please.

grammar.title: Polite Requests
grammar.ar: لطلب شيء بأدب شديد نستخدم I was wondering if you could + الفعل في المصدر. ورغم أن was في الماضي، فإن الطلب في الحاضر، واستخدام الماضي يجعل الطلب ألطف. ومع Would you mind نستخدم الفعل + ing، وإذا أردنا الموافقة نقول No, not at all لأن المعنى «هل تمانع؟».
examples: I was wondering if you could tell me where the train station is.
Would you mind helping me with my bag?
Would you mind waiting a few minutes?

words.ex: Al-Balad is the historic centre of Jeddah.
Kingdom Centre is a famous landmark in Riyadh.
These old houses date back to the 19th century.
Masmak Fortress is made of mud and stone.
The village is full of beautiful mud-brick buildings.
The king used to live in this palace.

dialogue.t: Welcome to Riyadh, everyone! Please follow me and stay together.
Thank you! Where are we going first?
We're starting in the old city. On your left you can see Masmak Fortress.
Wow, it looks very old. How old is it?
It dates back to the 1860s. It's one of the most important landmarks in Saudi history.
What is it made of?
It's made of mud-brick. Later, we'll visit Diriyah, which dates back to the 15th century.
Amazing! Can we take photos inside?

grammar.title: Describing Places and History
grammar.ar: نستخدم dates back to + سنة أو قرن لنقول إن مكاناً قديماً يعود إلى زمن معين، ويكون الفعل dates في المضارع البسيط لأن المكان ما زال موجوداً. ويمكن أيضاً استخدام المبني للمجهول في الماضي: It was built in + سنة. ولتوجيه السياح نستخدم عبارات مثل On your left/right you can see.
examples: On your right you can see the old market.
This mosque dates back to the 18th century.
The palace was built in 1936.

words.ex: I watch his travel vlog every Friday.
Don't forget to subscribe to my channel!
The view from the mountain is breathtaking.
The market gets very crowded in the evening.
Elephant Rock is a must-see in AlUla.
The highlight of our trip was the desert camp.

dialogue.t: Hi everyone! Today we're in AlUla with my brother, Omar. Say hi, Omar!
Hi everyone! It's so hot, but it's amazing here.
Right now, we're standing in front of Elephant Rock. Look how huge it is!
It really looks like an elephant. It's breathtaking!
So, Omar, what's the best thing here for you?
The best thing here is the sunset. The rocks turn orange and red.
I agree. It's definitely the highlight of our trip so far.
If you enjoyed this video, don't forget to like and subscribe. See you next time!

grammar.title: Present Continuous and Superlatives
grammar.ar: نستخدم المضارع المستمر (am/is/are + ing) لوصف ما يحدث الآن أثناء التصوير. وللقول إن شيئاً هو الأفضل أو الأكثر نستخدم صيغة التفضيل: the + صفة + est مثل the tallest، أو the most + صفة طويلة مثل the most beautiful. وانتبه إلى الصيغ الشاذة: good ← the best و bad ← the worst.
examples: We're walking through the old town right now.
The best thing here is the fresh seafood.
This is the most beautiful beach I've ever seen.

words.ex: Artificial intelligence helps doctors find diseases more quickly.
I ask my voice assistant about the weather every morning.
The app recommends songs that I might like.
Many people rely on maps on their phones when they travel.
Some people worry about their privacy when they use smart devices.
AI can translate a message into Arabic in seconds.

dialogue.t: Do you use AI at home?
Yes, all the time. AI is used to choose the videos I watch online.
Same here. My mum has a voice assistant. It makes cooking easier because it reads recipes aloud.
That's cool. In my house, AI is used to translate messages for my grandparents.
It makes communication easier, but sometimes the translations are really funny!
True. AI makes life easier, but I worry about our privacy.
Me too. Some apps collect a lot of information about us.
So we should use AI, but we should be careful.

grammar.title: is used to + verb / make + object + adjective
grammar.ar: نستخدم «is used to + فعل في المصدر» للتحدث عن الغرض من استخدام شيء ما، وهي صيغة المبني للمجهول في المضارع البسيط، مثل: AI is used to translate. انتبه: لا تخلطها مع «used to» التي تعني «اعتاد أن» في الماضي. ونستخدم «make + مفعول به + صفة» لوصف تأثير شيء ما، مثل: It makes homework easier. ونضيف «but» لذكر جانب سلبي.
examples: AI is used to recommend films on streaming apps.
Online maps make travelling easier, but they sometimes give wrong directions.
Smart cameras are used to recognise faces at airports.

words.ex: Who invented the telephone?
The smartphone is an amazing invention.
Penicillin was discovered by accident in 1928.
The printing press made books cheaper for everyone.
Today we can communicate with people all over the world.
Electric cars could change the way we travel.

dialogue.t: What do you think is the most important invention ever?
I think it's the internet. The first version of it was invented in the late 1960s.
Good choice. It has changed the way we learn and communicate.
Definitely. What about you?
I'd choose the printing press. It was invented by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440.
Why that one?
Because books were made faster and cheaper, so more people learned to read.
That's a great point. It has changed the way we share knowledge forever.

grammar.title: Past simple passive
grammar.ar: نستخدم المبني للمجهول عندما يكون الشيء أو الحدث أهم من الشخص الذي قام به. في الماضي البسيط نكوّنه بـ was/were + التصريف الثالث للفعل، مثل: The phone was invented. وإذا أردنا ذكر الفاعل نستخدم «by». تذكّر أنه لا يمكن حذف was/were في الجملة الإنجليزية.
examples: The light bulb was invented by Thomas Edison's team.
The first computers were built in the 1940s.
Television was invented in the 1920s, and it has changed the way we spend our free time.

words.ex: She wants a career in technology.
Robots might replace some factory workers.
Many supermarkets now have automated checkouts.
Coding is a useful skill for the future.
Data scientists are in demand all over the world.
Some old jobs will disappear because of new technology.

dialogue.t: What job do you want in the future?
I'm not sure. By 2040 many jobs will have disappeared, so it's hard to choose.
That's true. Robots will have replaced lots of factory workers by then.
But new jobs might appear too. Maybe I'll be a drone pilot!
Or a robot repair technician. New jobs might need skills we can't imagine yet.
I think creative jobs will still be in demand. Computers can't replace imagination easily.
I agree. By 2040 I will have finished university, so I'd better start learning to code now.
And languages too. Good communication will always be important.

grammar.title: Future perfect and might
grammar.ar: نستخدم المستقبل التام «will have + التصريف الثالث» للتحدث عن شيء سيكون قد اكتمل قبل وقت محدد في المستقبل، وغالباً نستخدم معه «by + زمن» مثل: By 2040. أما «might + فعل في المصدر» فنستخدمها للتعبير عن احتمال غير مؤكد في المستقبل. لا نضيف to بعد might.
examples: By 2040, self-driving cars will have changed the job of taxi drivers.
By the time I'm thirty, I will have worked in three different countries.
New jobs might include space tourism guides and AI trainers.

words.ex: We discussed the ethics of using AI in schools.
Never share your personal data with strangers online.
Apps should ask for permission before using your camera.
It's unfair if some students use AI to cheat in exams.
Some online videos can be harmful for young children.
Students aren't allowed to use phones during the test.

dialogue.t: Did you read the article about apps that collect children's data?
Yes! Companies shouldn't be allowed to collect our data without permission.
I agree, because that information could be used in a harmful way.
What about AI that writes homework? Should students be allowed to use it?
Maybe for ideas, but students shouldn't be allowed to copy answers, because it's unfair to others.
Good point. I also think companies shouldn't be allowed to make games that are too addictive.
Why not?
Because kids spend hours playing instead of sleeping or studying.

grammar.title: should / shouldn't be allowed to
grammar.ar: نستخدم «should be allowed to + فعل في المصدر» لنقول إنه من الصواب السماح بشيء ما، و«shouldn't be allowed to» لنقول إنه يجب منعه. هذه صيغة مبني للمجهول لأننا لا نذكر من يسمح أو يمنع. ونستخدم «because» بعدها لتوضيح السبب ودعم رأينا.
examples: Companies shouldn't be allowed to sell our personal information because it isn't safe.
Students should be allowed to use AI to check their spelling.
Robots shouldn't be allowed to make important medical decisions alone.

words.ex: My uncle loves buying new gadgets.
This watch features a heart-rate monitor.
The new phone has a long battery life.
You can swim with this waterproof camera.
The app is very user-friendly, even for my grandmother.
We want our gadget to be affordable for all students.

dialogue.t: Good morning, everyone. Let me introduce the SmartBag, a school bag that thinks for you.
Interesting! What can it do?
It features a GPS tracker, so you can't lose it, and a solar panel that charges your phone.
Is it heavy?
Not at all. It's light and waterproof. What makes it special is the voice reminder: it tells you if you've forgotten a book.
That's brilliant! How much does it cost?
It's affordable, about forty dollars. We think every student will want one.
I'd definitely buy one!

grammar.title: Emphasis with What ... is ...
grammar.ar: نستخدم تركيب «What + جملة + is ...» لنلفت انتباه المستمع إلى أهم فكرة، مثل: What makes it special is its design. هذا التركيب يجعل العرض التقديمي أقوى من الجملة العادية. نبدأ بـ What ثم الفعل، ثم is، ثم المعلومة المهمة التي نريد التركيز عليها.
examples: What makes it special is that it can recognise your voice.
What I love about this gadget is its long battery life.
What students need most is a tool that saves time.

words.ex: Four experts joined the panel to talk about AI.
She is an expert in robotics.
From my point of view, AI can help teachers.
Let's build on Sara's idea and make it better.
Omar raised an important issue about online safety.
AI is fast. On the other hand, it sometimes makes mistakes.

dialogue.t: From my point of view, AI tutors could help students who need extra support.
I'd like to add that they're available all day, unlike human teachers.
Exactly. Building on what you said, they could also help students in villages far from good schools.
That's a fair point. However, I'd like to raise one issue: not every family has fast internet.
True. Building on that, maybe governments should provide free internet in schools.
I'd like to add that teachers will still be important, because AI can't really understand feelings.
I completely agree. AI should support teachers, not replace them.

grammar.title: Adding to and building on ideas
grammar.ar: في النقاش نستخدم «I'd like to add that + جملة كاملة» لإضافة فكرة جديدة، و«I'd» هي اختصار «I would» وتجعل الكلام مهذباً. ونستخدم «Building on what you said, + جملة» لتطوير فكرة قالها شخص آخر. بعد هذه العبارات نحتاج دائماً إلى جملة فيها فاعل وفعل.
examples: I'd like to add that AI can help people with disabilities.
Building on what you said, schools could teach students how to use AI safely.
I'd like to add that we also need clear rules for technology companies.
